main_text.l: Ingreditur lectos, concubitusq; tuos: Secretum nihil est, tenebrosa cubilia pandit. Nox nihil inuoluet, nulla latebra teget. Huc ergo uenias, speculū uideasq; malorū, Hic & auos, proauos, hic atauosq; uide. Nunc uocat & reuocat panfis[?] Deus optimus Sancta flens urbe te cupit esse sua. (alis, Roma quidem ῥώμη[?] dicta est, sed noie uerso, Dici Roma potest improbitatis amor. Ah pigeat, pudeat: mores cum nomine muta: Roma ueni, ad Dnm uertere, Roma ueni. Si nil frontis habet meretrix, si stercora nolis Scire sciens: cogor dicere, Roma rues.
IN MINOTAVRVM ROMANVM, Carmen, autore Christ.Soth.

Credere quis posset (dictu est quoq; turpe) Roma pontifices esse, fuisse diu? (Priapos Nō soror hoc habitat Phoebi, nec Vesta, facello Amplius. Unde pbas? Stupra nefanda proque, mirū, quāta doctus grauitate Baleus (bat Depingit. nasum Rhinocerotis habet. Quicunq; ergo feris sublimi uertice fidus: Nunc caue ne titubes, Martia turba sapit. Nulla tibi tunica est parti obtendēda tegendę. Scorta impura magis non operire potes. Erumpet uox uera mihi, tibi faucibus haeret: Nō magis est sancti Roma cathedra Petri. Sed sedet hic fateor, quis? page.notes: The Greek word after "quidem" is printed small and is uncertain; read as ῥώμη. "panfis" is doubtful. "pbas?" and "Paulus. pernego. qs" are printed as shown, with a rule or mark between "Paulus." and "pernego." Small "<" marks stand beside two lines of the poem and are printer's pointing marks, not text. Underlining and smudges across the lines are not printed text. The first word of the second poem's stanza line is printed in italic-like type but is read as roman. The catchword and signature are at the lower edge; the signature mark is uncertain.
